newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer warned Bonn against reserve plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer warned Bonn against reserve plan - paper.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer warned the Bonn government earlier this year that any revaluation of its reserves could harm Germany's credibility, a German newspaper said on Tuesday.

Citing a confidential transcript, the Hannoversche Allgemeine Zeitung said Tietmeyer had on March 19 warned the government against "a change in the practice" under which the central bank values its currency and gold reserves at historical lows.
The newspaper distributed a summary of the article before publication.
It said Tietmeyer had argued that the Bundesbank's practice of valuing its reserves according to the lowest price principle had played an instrumental role in establishing credibility.
Any shift away from these methods now could unleash market turbulences, Tietmeyer was reported as saying.
"This topic should not be pulled onto the public stage during the delicate time before Europe's currency union in order to prevent market turbulences," the newspaper quoted him as saying.
He also said "the world's second largest reserve currency (is not underpinned) by national resources but solely by credibility."
The Bundesbank could not be reached for comment on the matter.

Talk about revaluing reserves has dominated Germany's political scene since mid-May when Finance Minister Theo Waigel announced the plan in what analysts said was a last-ditch effort to shore up Germany's ailing finances before currency union.
The Bundesbank council was expected to discuss the proposal at its council meeting on Wednesday and Waigel told journalists that a decision was expected.
He also said that an interim Bundesbank balance sheet has been drawn up and Bonn could receive a payout from a planned reserve revaluation during the course of this year.
Usually the government receives a portion of the Bundesbank profits in April of every year. Bonn has already received its portion of the 1996 profits.
